doc.title: Michael Max Fleming interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: Pay scales, unions and race in Cincinnati and New York
summary: White musicians were paid more and had a separate union. He talks about racial history, progress and the volatility of change.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Okay. You mentioned back in Cincinnati you had a pay scale for black musicians and a pay scale for white musicians.
Yeah but that was just between Kentucky and — but generally speaking, yes. The white musicians made more. Even their scale, we had two different unions.
Did the same thing happen in New York? © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

Yeah well that’s not music that’s just culturally the way things have evolved. You know. Queen Elizabeth, her son’s children, from where they had to go from where I had to go, it’s different because of the cultural — and it just happens to be — now if you go over to Egypt and your skin’s white, you might be a second-class citizen because you’re not the right religion. So it just happens that we’re talking about white and black. But it’s very clear how that is the way it is. George Washington, was he Chinese? Edison? Was he Jamaican? Was he from the Congo? Edison? Even though there were people there who were working under him who had very bright people, very black, bright black people that helped him invent some of the things that he got credit for. But because of the way things were set up socially, anthropologically, that’s the way it is. I mean it’s obvious and I don’t grieve over it because it won’t make a difference, to grieve over it. But it’s obvious that’s the way it is. You know? And that’s the way it is. And that has been our history. It doesn’t mean there it is, and it’s not stagnant, it’s changed. There has been progress. We had a black president. How about that. We had Jackie Robinson. How about that. So it’s changing. But if you just open your eyes, I mean we don’t have to have a debate, a formal debate over — that’s the way it is, man.

Do you think it will always be that way? No, well, I apologize, because you already answered that question. You’re talking about a progression. And just because something is the way it is now, it may change. But —

Unfortunately, how about this, which is a big part of the hysteria. What if it evolves to the roles are reversed? And it may be, sure. But I’m not saying that’s the way it’s going to be. But I’m just saying that’s the nature of how things evolve and change. It’s that volatile. One event can mess everything up, man, or change everything. One event. One dumb, stupid move. Yeah. I’m not saying it’s dumb for it to be reversed. I just want people to get along. So I’m not interested in — that’s all. Do I want to be king? Yeah, sign me up.
